panels.rationale: Single-panel axial MRI (T2/STIR-type sequence) of the neck showing a hyperintense cystic mass in the right cervical region, consistent with the captioned lymphatic malformation with intracapsular hemorrhage. The figure comes from a CLAPO syndrome case report (a PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum subtype), and the caption and in-text explicitly attribute this lymphatic malformation to the patient, making disease attribution solid. Lymphatic malformation is a hallmark feature of CLAPO syndrome, so typicality is classic. Patient age 3 years 6 months supports child age group. No skin visible, no ethnicity stated, no annotations. Intracapsular hemorrhage is clearly present on the image but is not covered by the vocabulary, so it is listed as a proposed finding. [raw subtype: CLAPO syndrome]

in_text_mentions: the cervical region, as seen on DSA angiography and MRI (Figure 2). At 3 years and 6 months, a 2 cm diameter mass suddenly appeared in her right neck, which ultrasound and MRI indicated as a lymphatic malformation with intracapsular hemorrhage (Figure 3). Ultrasound-guided extraction of the lymphatic sac effusion (6 mL) was followed by injection of 1 mg of pingyangmycin for sclerotherapy. She has not presented any neurological symptoms or intellectual disability up to age 4. Unfortunately, genetic testing was recommended for the child, but her parents did not agree to the test due to the cost.
